title: What is the smallest angle that stops the two arms meeting?
description: The angle at one end of the base is forty degrees. The arm from the other end is turned outwards until it just stops meeting the first arm, and that arm is parallel to the first. Keeko's doubt is that a longer base changes the smallest angle.
teaching_notes: One idea: the arm that leans least and does not meet the first arm is parallel to it, so the two angles at the base add to one hundred and eighty degrees. Watch for students who think the length of the base matters.

source: The angle at A is 40°. Find the smallest angle at B for which the arms from A and B do not meet, and say whether the length AB matters.
video_script.why: The child knows that two angles of ninety degrees or more give no triangle and now finds the exact smallest angle that stops the arms meeting.
video_script.substitution: The book's own angle of forty degrees at A, with the arm from B turned outwards.
video_script.anchor: a base AB with an angle of forty degrees at A and an arm from B that is turned outwards
video_script.wrong_answer: a longer base changes the smallest angle at B
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko stretches the base longer and expects the smallest angle at B to change, but the limit arm stays parallel to the first arm whatever the base, so the angle does not change.
video_script.payoff_line: The smallest angle at bee is one hundred and forty degrees

final_answer.spoken: the smallest angle at bee is one hundred and forty degrees, and the length of eigh bee does not matter

maths_rules: the arm from B that leans least and still does not meet the arm from A is the line m parallel to l
AB is a transversal of the parallel lines l and m, and the inside angles on the same side add up to 180°
an angle B of 140° or more does not meet l, and an angle B below 140° does meet l
the length AB is not used in any step, so it does not matter
video_script.design: One base AB with the 40 degree arm l is drawn. The arm from B is swung outwards until it is parallel to l, and AB is shown as the transversal. Then the base is stretched to show the angle does not change.

narration: <bookmark mark='par'/>Two lines that stay the same distance apart and never meet are called parallel.
<bookmark mark='trans'/>A line that cuts across two parallel lines is called a transversal.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The two inside angles on the same side of a transversal add to one hundred and eighty degrees.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The smallest angle at bee is one hundred and forty degrees.
